answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. Consider a jetty as the anchor of the cost.
